t: A Level Far From Spot Is Not a Broken Calculation

t: A Deep Pool That Trades Badly
d: Total value locked is not tradeable depth. Several structures produce a large headline number and poor execution at any size that matters.

t: Why Are My Options So Expensive? (It's Usually IV)
d: Options feel expensive mostly because of high implied volatility, which inflates premiums before events and in volatile markets. Here's what actually makes options.

t: Why ATM Options Have the Most Gamma (and the Most Whip)
d: Delta barely budges deep in or far out of the money. Right at the strike it swings hardest, and that rate of change is gamma, the source of 0DTE whip.

t: Automation Isn't Passive
d: A system takes away the watching, clicking, and fatigue, not the responsibility of running it. Where the work actually moves once execution is automated.

t: Why You Should Avoid Trading the Very First Minute
d: The opening auction has just cleared and price is hunting fair value with wide spreads and no structure yet. Waiting a few minutes is one of the cheapest edges.

t: Why Can't I Sell My Option? Wide Spreads and Thin Liquidity
d: If you're struggling to sell an option at a fair price, the culprit is usually thin liquidity — a wide bid-ask spread with few buyers.

t: Consistency Beats Being Right
d: You don't need to be right often to make money — you need a consistent process with positive expectancy, repeated.

t: Why a Crypto Drawdown Feels Worse Than the Same Percentage Elsewhere
d: Continuous trading means you watch every hour of it. The number is comparable; the experience is not, and the experience is what breaks plans.

t: Crypto Gamma Is Smaller Than It Looks
d: Options open interest in crypto is large in absolute terms and small relative to spot turnover. That ratio, not the headline, decides whether dealers can move price.

t: Why Crypto Options Are Quoted in Volatility
d: Traders quote each other in vol rather than in dollars because vol is the part of the price that carries an opinion. Everything else is arithmetic.

t: Spreads Widen Exactly When You Need Them Tight
d: Market makers widen as uncertainty rises, so the cost of trading peaks during the moves that make you want to trade. That is rational, not hostile.

t: Why Volatility Clusters, and What Sustains It in Crypto
d: Big moves follow big moves in every market. In crypto the mechanism is largely leverage, which makes the clustering sharper and shorter.

t: Why Dealers End Up Short Puts (and What It Does to the Floor)
d: Hedgers buy protection persistently, so dealers carry the other side. That short-put position is the mechanical floor at the put wall, and the danger below it.

t: Why Did Implied Volatility Drop and Sink My Option?
d: Implied volatility often collapses after an event resolves — the 'IV crush' — deflating your option's value even if the underlying moved your way.

t: Why Did My Option Expire Worthless?
d: An option expires worthless when it finishes out-of-the-money — the underlying never reached your strike, so there's no value left.

t: Why Did My Fill Price Differ From the Quote?
d: Your order filled at a slightly different price than the quote you saw — that's slippage, and it's normal.

t: Why Funding Should Never Be Blended Across Venues
d: Averaging funding across exchanges destroys the only thing it was telling you. The disagreement between venues is the signal, not noise to be smoothed away.

t: Why Gamma Matters for 0DTE
